content:
Motivation: sphere packing (compare. Flyspeck project), square packing (e.g. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0097316575900990 , 57 cites), other types (the book "Unsolved problems in geometry" has a whole section dedicated to packing/covering problem). In developing this, it's likely one would need to develop a library of geometric algorithms (and prove their correctness) as well.
One possible counterargument is that this doesn't really have further application.
In term of generality, I think formalizing a (e.g. square) packing as a isometric embedding from a disjoint union of N unit squares to a Riemannian manifold isomorphic to a large square would be sufficiently general. (Advantage of using Riemannian manifold is one can talk about embedding in e.g. hyperbolic space as well.) (Thinking about it, I wonder if packing works in p-adic manifold...)
Thoughts?
